audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Quinn/Quinn/Skill/Skill/Quinn/Quinn — it called Level 1 even and handed Quinn both First item and 2+ items.
audit.why: 49.29% over 493 games; the packet chart is Quinn rows 0-2, Skill rows 3-5, Wukong row 6. The page's own spikes and late text say Wukong fully outscales at two items and that the first-item window is only even, so three rows contradicted the prose next to them.
audit.corrected: Quinn rows 0-2, Skill rows 3-5, Wukong row 6, both layers.

audit.why: Level 6 Cyclone and the 2-item bruiser window are the correct spikes, and the early poke window pre-Nimbus Strike is real. Left the spike entries alone apart from naming.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow is never identified as an auto-attack reset, and nothing warns that Cyclone's knockup cancels Behind Enemy Lines. Only Nimbus Strike was ever named.
audit.why: Quinn's R carries 'channel — interruptible, any CC cancels it', and the page itself already describes Cyclone as a spin-knockup, so starting the channel while he holds it throws the ultimate away. Crushing Blow opening with an auto reset means the wind-up, not the cast, is the moment to step back.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto reset — read the wind-up. Cyclone's knockup cancels your R channel, so never start it while Cyclone is up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole content layer is first person ('Levels 1-3 are mine', 'kills me through everything').
audit.why: Breaks the second-person voice used across the site.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[0..6], early, mid and late in second person with the real ability names.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[0].d ('That is Wukong's favourite window...') and dontsFull[1].d ('Burning it for tiny value...') are both template filler that never mention the decoy or the armour shred their headings promise.
audit.corrected: Decoy body for the clone don't; Crushing Blow body for the shred don't.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are mine. My range and Harrier auto-resets out-trade him before his Q armor-shred ramps and his E dash is up — poke him with the bird ball (Q) every time he steps to last-hit. Don't waste E early; save it to disengage if he dashes in. He has no real kill pressure on me until 6, so just stack the poke and deny his CS.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are yours. Your range and Harrier auto-resets out-trade him before Crushing Blow's armour shred ramps and Nimbus Strike is up — poke with Blinding Assault every time he steps to last-hit. Do not waste Vault early; save it to disengage the dash. He has no kill pressure until Cyclone, so stack poke and deny his CS.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 it evens out. The moment he hits 6, his E-dash into R spin-knockup can airborne me and chunk me before I reposition, so respect that all-in and keep W ready to kite the follow-up. Bait his E by hovering just out of dash range, blind-poke with Q, and only Vault (E) in once his dash is on cooldown. Watch the W clone — don't blow my combo on the decoy.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 it evens out. The moment he hits 6, Nimbus Strike into Cyclone knocks you airborne and chunks you before you reposition — and that knockup cancels your R channel, so never start it while Cyclone is up. Bait the dash by hovering just outside its range, blind-poke, and Vault in only once it is spent. Watch the Warrior Trickster decoy.

edits.before: Late, he wins. Once he stacks armor and bruiser items his E-R commit kills me through everything, and I'm too squishy to trade back front-to-front. My only out is to have already snowballed — shove, roam with R, and pick his team instead of dueling him. If the game goes long even, he flips it; close it before 2+ items land.
edits.after: Late, he wins. Once he stacks armour and bruiser items his Nimbus Strike into Cyclone commit kills you through everything, and you are too squishy to trade front-to-front. Your only out is to have already snowballed — shove, roam with R, and pick off his team instead of dueling him. Close it before his second item lands.

notes: enemyKit was null for Wukong in this brief, so no cooldown or range numbers were available — every claim here is from the packet ability list, the missing-interactions file, or Quinn's own kit. Nothing numeric was invented. Quinn's Heightened Senses carries a revealsStealth flag and Warrior Trickster grants brief invisibility; whether the reveal actually defeats it is not in either file, so I left it out. Also: the item line recommends anti-heal 'his healing fights your pattern' — Wukong has no healing in the packet ability list, so that clause looks like boilerplate carried in from another matchup and is worth a manual check.
